same underlying bug as #15059. also fires with no plugins installed — opencode's title-generator path emits two role: "system" entries on its own (title-generator prompt + inherited delegation block) on the first call of any session against a Qwen 3.5+ deployment.

confirmed against **Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B** and **Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B** on **vLLM v0.21.0** with **opencode v1.14.39**, vanilla install. the superpowers/opencode-dcp/llama-server reports are the same path made more visible by extra system fragments, not a separate bug.

diagnosis, fix snippet, and currently-open PR (#16981) tracked in #15059.

same root cause as #15059. the qwen 3.6 chat template raises raise_exception('System message must be at the beginning.') when messages[] contains more than one role: "system". image input isn't what triggers it, just tends to coincide with the second system fragment being added.

opencode's title-generator path produces two consecutive system entries even on vanilla installs. diagnosis + fix snippet in #15059, currently-open PR is #16981.

same bug as #15059. @paulgear's #15018 was the right shape, and #16981 (currently open and awaiting code-owner review) generalizes it with a capability flag.

still broken on opencode v1.14.39 against Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on vLLM v0.21.0, even with no plugins — the title-generator path produces [system, system, user] on its own. running the equivalent of #15018 locally resolves the 400s without affecting any other provider.

diagnosis + repro in #15059.

patch shape here is correct (system.join collapsing the array at dispatch). running the equivalent locally to keep Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B working under opencode v1.14.39, no impact on other providers. auto-close was template-compliance, not code review.

note for anyone picking this up: 

 reads better than 
 — paragraph separator preserves section structure in templates that treat blank lines as breaks. either clears the qwen guard. currently-open generalization is #16981.

+1 to @draxxris's question. running the equivalent merge locally for opencode v1.14.x against Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on vLLM v0.21.0. no regression on anthropic or any other provider.

framing here ("non-anthropic providers") read as more conditional than the change actually is: OpenAI's Chat Completions contract treats messages[] as expecting one system entry, and anthropic prompt caching uses a separate system parameter on a different SDK path, so an unconditional merge at the messages[] assembly site doesn't regress anthropic.

#16981 is currently open and waiting on code-owner review with the same fix generalized as a systemMessage: 'single' | 'multiple' capability flag.

The remaining sharp edge here looks less like "how large should the defaults be?" and more like "does the model see the effective execution contract it is about to override?"

If the operator sets a two-hour shell default plus larger `tool_output` limits, the agent still needs a machine-visible receipt before it chooses an explicit shorter timeout: effective timeout, effective max lines/bytes, persisted output path, and a recommended next action such as `read_saved_output` versus `rerun_command`. Without that, the model can accidentally turn an operator-level policy into a smaller per-call timeout and recreate the retry loop.

In MartinLoop terms, I would treat truncated output or timeout as an admission decision for the next attempt: rerun only if the command or failure class changed; otherwise read the saved artifact. That might be a small fixture worth adding around this issue: "large output saved, assistant's next step reads the saved path instead of rerunning."

Closing as duplicate of #28846. Consolidating discussion there.

Here is a detailed reverse-calculation confirming the issue, with references.

**DeepSeek V4 Pro official pricing timeline**

| Date | Change | Cache Hit (per 1M) | Cache Miss (per 1M) | Output (per 1M) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apr 24 (launch) | Original pricing | $0.145 | $1.74 | $3.48 |
| Apr 26 | Cache hit reduced to 1/10 | $0.0145 | $1.74 | $3.48 |
| Apr 26 | V4 Pro 75% off starts | $0.003625 | $0.435 | $0.87 |
| **May 22** | **75% made permanent** | **$0.003625** | **$0.435** | **$0.87** |

**What OpenCode Go currently charges (reverse-calculated)**

From the Go docs (updated May 23, still showing old quotas):
- 3,450 requests per 5h
- 750 input (cache miss) + 82,000 cached + 290 output tokens per request
- $12/5h limit

| Item | Per-request tokens | Implied price | Per-request cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cache miss input | 750 | **$1.74/M (original)** | $0.001305 |
| Cache hit input | 82,000 | **$0.0145/M (1/10 cache reduction only)** | $0.001189 |
| Output | 290 | **$3.48/M (original)** | $0.001009 |
| **Total** | 83,040 | | **~$0.00350** |

3,450 × $0.00350 = $12.08 ≈ $12/5h ✓

**At the current permanent discounted price (~$0.000876/request), the same $12 should allow ~13,700 requests — 75% more than the current 3,450.**

**Also worth noting:** OpenCode has adjusted these numbers before. Commit #24575 (Apr 27) increased V4 Pro from 1,300 to 3,450 after DeepSeek reduced cache hit pricing. So the mechanism exists — it just hasnt been applied to the 75% discount.

Closing as duplicate of #7101, which proposes the same core feature (custom system prompts with proper precedence hierarchy). Our use case — enforcing project-level language/behavior directives that override the default Role block — is covered by #7101's proposal for project-instance prompts at `.opencode/prompt/`.
Duplicate of #7101

## +1 from a concrete use case

Our scenario: a non-English team needs project-level behavioral directives (e.g., \"always reply in Traditional Chinese\") that reliably override the default Role block.

### The specific problem

The current precedence chain puts AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md below the Role block:

```
Bundled system prompts (lowest)
  → Global config
    → Project-level config
      → AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md (project context)
        → Role block (agent identity, wins)
          → User message
```

Even when AGENTS.md explicitly states the reply language, the agent defaults to English because the Role defines identity in English. The behavioral directive and the identity conflict, and identity wins.

### Why `instructions` alone isn't enough

The existing `opencode.json` → `instructions[]` array loads additional files, but they're injected at the same precedence level as AGENTS.md — still below the Role block. What's needed is a mechanism that injects at a level **above** the Role block, so behavioral rules can override identity defaults.

### Suggestion

Your proposal of `~/.config/opencode/prompt/` and `<project>/.opencode/prompt/` with clear precedence ordering would solve this perfectly. The key requirement is that the **project-level custom prompt has higher precedence than the bundled Role block**, so users can reliably override agent behavior without editing the bundled prompts.

We can confirm the empty-parts pattern from the plugin side. While building the MCP Memory Service plugin for OpenCode, we traced through the plugin loader source (`packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts`) and found that `chat.message` is not triggered at all in some builds — the `trigger("chat.message", ...)` call site doesn't exist in the session processor.

**Workaround**: use the `event` hook with bus subscription to listen for `message.part.updated` bus events. These carry the full text content in `event.properties.part.text` for TextPart and ReasoningPart objects.

Working plugin (820 lines, zero external deps): https://github.com/doobidoo/mcp-memory-service/blob/main/opencode/memory-plugin.js

Hooks we use:
- `event` — catches `message.part.updated`, `session.created`, `session.deleted`
- `experimental.chat.system.transform` — memory injection into system prompt
- `experimental.session.compacting` — memory preservation

Also opened #29022 with more context.

@anomalyco/maintainers — this isn't a vanity post. It documents a gap in the plugin docs:

- `chat.message` is listed in `@opencode-ai/plugin` Hooks interface but **never triggered** by the session processor
- We traced through `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts` to confirm
- The `event` hook (bus subscription) is the only way to capture message content — and this isn't documented either

This directly relates to #22831 (feature request to expose body to chat.message) and #23440 (chat.message crash). We've added our findings with concrete workarounds to both.

If this issue type isn't supported, that's fine — the information is already linked from the related issues. But it would be useful for other plugin developers who hit the same dead end.
